title: Historic Sussex pub and hotel said to be one of the most haunted in the UK
excerpt: The Mermaid Inn, a Grade II listed building in Rye, has a reputation as one of the UK's most haunted inns.
content:
One of England’s most famously haunted pubs is in Sussex and continues to intrigue visitors with chilling tales of ghostly encounters.

The Mermaid Inn, a Grade II listed building in Rye, East Sussex, dates back to the 12th century and is known not only for its long, colourful history but also for its reputation as one of the UK's most haunted inns.

The current structure was rebuilt in 1420, with cellars that date back to 1156.

Visitors and staff alike have reported unexplained phenomena throughout the inn’s rooms, and some refuse to enter certain areas alone.

Is the Mermaid Inn in Rye haunted?

Guests who have stayed at the Mermaid Inn have shared several stories of ghostly encounters.

Room 17 is among the most notorious.

It is said to turn icy cold without warning, and a rocking chair is reported to move on its own.

Chambermaids reportedly refuse to enter the room alone, choosing instead to clean it in pairs.

Guests have also sent in photographs showing mysterious orbs floating around the room.

Other reports describe the room dividing into zones of extreme heat and cold.

Room 5 is haunted by a "Lady in White," who is said to pass through the room and pause briefly at the foot of the bed.

Room 3 was the site of a more physical encounter.

A guest staying there reported feeling as though he had been kicked in the back while his wife was in the bathroom.

He described being overcome by a sense of well-being immediately afterward, and said everything returned to normal when his wife re-entered the room.

Room 10 is linked to one of the inn’s most dramatic ghost stories.

A bank manager and his wife reported waking in the night to see a man walk through their bathroom wall and across the room.

The couple was so frightened that they spent the rest of the night in one of the downstairs lounges, and made the porter bring all their luggage downstairs, plus their clothes.

The Mermaid Inn’s history is filled with colourful characters, both living and spectral.

Famous guests have included Lord Alfred Douglas, F.E. Smith, Henry Dodge, Ford Madox Ford, Dame Ellen Terry, Hilaire Belloc, Henry James, Rupert Travers, and Ben Travers.

Actress Kiki Kendrick and her husband Robin also experienced what they believe was a ghostly encounter during a stay at the inn.

Ms Kendrick said: "In December 1993 we had booked 4 nights in the Elizabethan Bedchamber.

"It was our first ever visit to Rye.

"We knew nothing about The Mermaid’s Ghosts or that it was even haunted.

"On our first night after a couple of drinks in the bar, we retired to our room at about midnight.

"Around 4.00am suddenly and for no reason, we both sat bolt upright in bed.

"There was an eerie presence.

"The warm and toasty room had suddenly turned strangely cold and we could hear a fight going on in the corner of the room.

"By the fireplace there were huffs and puffs and sounds of clashing knives.

"We could see shapes moving, as if looking through opaque glass.

"They fought violently.

"It was very scary."

The couple shared their experience with a member of staff the next evening.

Ms Kendrick said: "The next evening, we told the barman and he produced an old newspaper article about ghosts in the Elizabethan Bedchamber that had been written by 2 journalists who had stayed there 6 months earlier.

"It read word for word as we had seen it."

The following night, the same scene played out again, though only Ms Kendrick witnessed it.

She said that they have stayed in the same room since but have not experienced anything similar.

The Mermaid Inn has also been featured on the TV series Most Haunted, further cementing its reputation as a destination for those seeking a brush with the supernatural.
